# /api/sessions/active docstring still states the pre-09-07 allow-list, contradicting the NON_USER_PLATFORMS deny-list

Found reviewing architecture/ambient-context-injection.md

The doc states `NON_USER_PLATFORMS` + `is_user_session` "are the one definition now". They are not: the `/api/sessions/active` handler's own docstring restates the **pre-2026-09-07 allow-list** and contradicts it.

`app/routers/sessions.py:989-996`:
```
  2. Most-recent `platform: mission-control` session by mtime (≤24h)
  ...
Explicitly excludes `platform: autonomy` sessions so an autonomy task
never gets its own session back.
```
The implementation is a deny-list: `NON_USER_PLATFORMS = frozenset({"autonomy", "worker"})` (`app/sessions_io.py:94`) applied through `is_user_session` on **both** rules — the in-memory hint re-validation (`:245-253`) and the mtime scan (`:259-268`). `worker` is excluded and unknown platforms stay eligible, which `tests/test_active_session_resolution.py::test_an_unknown_platform_stays_eligible` and `::test_rule_two_skips_worker_and_autonomy` pin.

Why it matters: this is the text an operator reads when a producer reports "no active user session", and it is the text an editor edits against. Re-narrowing to the docstring's literal allow-list would silently stop delivering briefs to any platform not named `mission-control` — precisely the failure the deny-list comment at `app/sessions_io.py:85-93` exists to prevent, and it would pass tests only if those two cases were changed too.

Fix: rewrite the docstring to name the deny-list and defer to `is_user_session` rather than re-listing platforms. Proving: `sed -n '985,1002p' app/routers/sessions.py` against `sed -n '85,99p;228,270p' app/sessions_io.py`.

## Merged finding — 2026-09-12

_Filed as "/api/sessions/create takes `platform` unchecked, so 49 bench sessions read as user chats and get exported and embedded" by session 20260912_190705_archreview_0cbf; merged here by write-time dedupe (rule A, score 1.0, lexical 0.247). Re-file with `force: true` if this is a distinct finding._

Found reviewing architecture/background-runs.md

`app/sessions_io.py:94` `NON_USER_PLATFORMS = frozenset({"autonomy", "worker"})` is the one definition of "nobody reads this session", and §8's whole bounding argument depends on it. It has an unvalidated hole: `POST /api/sessions/create` (`app/routers/sessions.py:564`) takes `platform` straight from the request body — its own docstring lists only `mission-control | autonomy | inner_voice`, and nothing checks the value against anything. **49 files in `lloyd/sessions/` carry `platform: browser`**, ids `<ts>_iv<4hex>`, each with 1 message and `inner_voice: true` — the Inner Voice bench harness creating a session per trial. Measured today: worker 1007, autonomy 229, mission-control 107, browser 49.

Because `"browser" not in NON_USER_PLATFORMS`, `is_user_session` returns True, so each trial's turn is: listed in `/api/sessions` (chat history, visible to the user as something they said), counted by `_scan_recent_sessions`, and exported by `app/post_capture.py:293-295` into `_pipeline/vault-derived/sessions-background/` — the export split also keys off `is_user_session`, so these land on the *user* side of it and are picked up by `agent-services/scripts/qmd-watcher.sh`, which indexes and embeds `sessions/`. That is the exact cost the §8 export split exists to prevent: machine-run bench turns entering the corpus that answers "what did Lloyd and the user discuss", one embedded document per bench trial, and the §8 "~14 chats a day" denominator is 49 files wrong.

Fix shape: validate `platform` in `/api/sessions/create` against a named set (the docstring's three values, plus `worker`/`autonomy`), reject or coerce anything else, and have the bench harness pass a non-user platform. A cheap companion guard belongs in `tests/test_session_platform_checks.py`, which already sweeps the session-id creation sites: assert every `platform` value present in the live session directory is either in `NON_USER_PLATFORMS` or one of the two user-facing names, so a new producer that invents a platform is caught rather than silently becoming a chat.

item.name: Background-task notifications are unreachable inside a Task subagent — its per-session drain queue is never drained
item.body:
# Background-task notifications are unreachable inside a Task subagent — its per-session drain queue is never drained

Split from #411 during automod triage on 2026-09-11.

## Claim
A `Task` subagent that starts a background Bash command is promised a `<task_notification>` it can never receive. Completion records are queued per-session and delivered only by `RunOptions.notification_drain`, which is wired for chat turns and never for a subagent — and the subagent's session id is its own `task:<type>:<hex>`, so its queue is drained by nobody. Because `Task` blocks its caller until the child returns, there is also no "later turn" for the notification to surface in.

## Current state (verified 2026-09-11)
- `RunOptions.notification_drain` is declared at `app/harness/options.py:129` and consumed by the loop every iteration at `app/harness/loop.py:235-245` (`chat_messages.extend(drained)`).
- It is set in exactly one place in production: `app/routers/messages.py:859` → `options.notification_drain = _build_notification_drain(session_id, turn.turn_id)` (builder at `app/routers/messages.py:513-545`, which calls the internal `_BackgroundTaskDrain` tool with `session_id` in `_meta`).
- The subagent's `RunOptions(...)` at `agent_mcp/builtin_task.py:223-256` sets model, base_url, system_prompt, max_turns, disallowed_tools, hooks, mcp_servers, session_id, preserve_thinking_iterations, stream_chunk_timeout_s, parallel_tool_calls_enabled/max_concurrency — **no `notification_drain`, no `state_anchor`**.
- Queueing is per-session: `agent_mcp/builtin_bash.py:246` `session_id = get_bound_session()`, waiter enqueues at `_task_registry.start_waiter` / `_await_and_complete` (`agent_mcp/_task_registry.py:199-213`), drained by `drain_completed_for_session(session_id)` (`agent_mcp/_task_registry.py:271`, called from `builtin_bash.py:289-290`).
- The subagent's session id is minted at `agent_mcp/builtin_task.py:220-221` as `task:{subagent_type}:{uuid}` — a queue key no caller ever passes to `_BackgroundTaskDrain`.
- `general-purpose` has `disallowed_tools: []` (`config.yaml:434-442`), so Bash with `run_in_background=true` is available inside a Task, and `builtin_bash.py:275` / `:348` tell the child model "A <task_notification> will appear on a later turn" — for a subagent that sentence is false.

## Check that shows it
```
grep -rn "notification_drain" --include=*.py ~/lloyd | grep -v "/tests/\|test_"
#   options.py:129 (decl), loop.py:235-239 (consume), messages.py:513/859 (the only wire-up)
#   → zero hits under agent_mcp/builtin_task.py
grep -n "notification_drain\|state_anchor" ~/lloyd/agent_mcp/builtin_task.py   # 0 hits
```

## Fix shape (not pre-decided)
Give the child's `RunOptions` a drain closure over the child's own session id (the same `_build_notification_drain` shape, or a child-side equivalent that does not persist to a chat session JSON — note `_build_notification_drain` also writes a `source: "bg_task_notification"` session message, which has no home for a subagent). Decide explicitly whether a child's late notification should instead be routed to `record.parent_turn_id` (`agent_mcp/_subagent_registry.py:55`, whose comment already says late arrivals "have to reach the parent"). Related but separate: `state_anchor` is likewise unset for subagents (`app/routers/messages.py:2078` is the only wire-up) so a child never gets todo/plan re-anchoring — same RunOptions construction site, different consequence; decide it in the same pass.

## Acceptance
- A test spawns a `Task` whose fake run_query yields a Bash background start, the registry completes it, and the child's next iteration sees a `<task_notification>` message (mirror the drain assertions used for the primary turn).
- The same test asserts the notification is not lost silently: if the chosen design routes it to the parent, the parent-visible artifact is asserted instead.
